mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate at a New Zealand notary public; if the destination country is party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, submit the notarised document to the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Authentication Unit for a single apostille certificate. If the destination country is not an Apostille Convention member, submit the notarised document to MFAT for authentication and then to the embassy or consulate of the destination country for consular legalization. These protocols are parallel and mutually exclusive; apostille and consular legalization must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, the incorporating agent and the reporting entity must screen all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, company secretaries, authorised signatories, counterparties, vessels, consignees, and intermediaries against the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2022 designations, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, United Kingdom sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT indicators, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit alerts. Politically exposed persons must be identified using a risk-based approach covering family members and close associates; all PEP matches must trigger enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Daily screening and adverse media review must be applied to all high-risk jurisdictions, scrap metal trading routes, and documentary letter of credit and SWIFT telegraphic transfer payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Company Register and Name Reservation Service (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Maori using Latin alphabetic characters; non-Latin script names must be transliterated phonetically into Latin script. The Companies Office requires the legal element Limited or Ltd to appear at the end of the name, and the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name. The four-tier naming convention applied is: (1) identity and similarity review against the Companies Register; (2) offensiveness and deception assessment; (3) prior consent or ministerial approval for restricted tokens; and (4) final section 22 Companies Act 1993 compliance and availability reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the New Zealand Companies Office rejects a reserved name, the applicant must receive a written refusal quoting section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 and the specific ground for refusal. The applicant may apply for an administrative reconsideration by the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of refusal, attaching the refusal notice, the original name reservation application, consent letters from any relevant Minister or regulator for restricted tokens, and a legal submission demonstrating that the name is not offensive, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name. The Registrar must issue a reconsideration decision within 10 working days. A name reservation cannot be extended; if the 20-working-day reservation lapses, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation application, but priority is lost if the name has been taken by a third party in the meantime. If the Registrar sustains the refusal after internal reconsideration, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review of the Registrar's decision in the High Court of New Zealand under the Senior Courts Act 2016, naming the Registrar of Companies as respondent and providing evidence of standing and the decision under review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may satisfy the Companies Act 1993 requirement for a registered office in New Zealand if it is a physical New Zealand street address, not a post office box, at which documents can be served and received during business hours. However, for the recycling and physical consignment of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire under ISIC 4669, this structure will face material bank and Inland Revenue Department substance scrutiny. New Zealand banks and the IRD are likely to reject a pure commercial mail forwarding box without records of staff, a lease, board meeting facilities, physical inventory, and trade documentation. A serviced office with a dedicated physical suite, a named local registered agent, storage and inspection arrangements, and customs compliance infrastructure is more likely to be accepted. A non-physical virtual office alone is insufficient for AML/CFT customer due diligence and is an adverse indicator for cross-border B2B metals trading because of the high money laundering and trade-based money laundering risk in the scrap metal sector.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for announced and unannounced inspections by IRD, the New Zealand Companies Office, and customs authorities: (i) physical signboard at the registered address; (ii) presence of staff able to accept service and answer inquiries; (iii) lease or tenancy agreement covering the registered office; (iv) access to corporate records and board meeting facilities; (v) dedicated business telephone and email; (vi) IRD correspondence address and GST compliance records; (vii) bank account statement address matching the registered office; (viii) customs and export records for scrap copper wire; (ix) warehouse receipts, logistics contracts, insurance policies and supplier agreements evidencing real commercial substance. Quantified risk: high, estimated at 65-70%, of an unannounced physical inspection by the IRD or the Companies Office within the first 18 months of operation because the business is an export-oriented physical commodities trader; the likelihood rises to 80% or higher if the registered office is a pure virtual mailbox with no physical premises or personnel, and when using documentary letters of credit and SWIFT telegraphic transfers as the primary payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), being Public Act 1993 No 105, and the Companies (Incorporation and Constitutional Documents) Regulations 1993. Applicable sections include s 15 (registration of companies), s 12 and s 13 (company names), s 30 (registered office), s 42 and s 44 (directors), s 51 and s 52 (consents and director certification), s 81 and s 82 (share capital and allotment), s 122 (board resolutions), s 128 and s 129 (powers of the board), s 189 (director duties), and Part 23 (annual return and disclosure obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Incorporation of a Company submitted through the New Zealand Companies Office portal pursuant to s 15 of the Companies Act 1993, which generates the Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law prescribes no minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company. The board may issue shares for no paid-up capital or for such consideration as it determines, provided shares are not issued at a discount and the board complies with any solvency requirements under the Companies Act 1993. No statutory escrow or blocked share capital account is required, and the registered share capital will be shown in the company's annual return.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, ADOPTED ON [DATE] 20[YEAR], PURSUANT TO THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 AND THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMPANY.
1. CONSTITUTION: IT IS RESOLVED that the constitution filed with the application for incorporation is adopted as the constitution of the Company in its entirety. Each director, shareholder, and officer shall comply with its provisions. The directors are authorised to file consents and notices in the Companies Register as required by the Registrar.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE: IT IS RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [ADDRESS], New Zealand, being a physical place within New Zealand, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified. The directors are authorised to change the registered office from time to time, subject to written notice to the Registrar.
3. SHARE CAPITAL AND ALLOTMENT: IT IS RESOLVED that the share capital of the Company consists of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value. The board hereby allots [NUMBER] ordinary shares to the incorporator for a consideration of NZD [AMOUNT], to be satisfied by cash or capitalised shareholder loan. The directors are directed to complete the share register, issue share certificates, and ensure that no future allotment contravenes the Companies Act 1993. No shares shall be issued at a discount.
4. BANKING ARRANGEMENTS: IT IS RESOLVED that corporate banking accounts be opened with [BANK NAME], New Zealand Branch. The directors named as [DIRECTOR A] and [DIRECTOR B] are appointed authorised signatories, and any two signing jointly may draw cheques, give receipts, releases, indemnities, and banking instructions, including electronic wire transfers, SWIFT TT, and documentary credit instructions. This mandate remains valid until revoked in writing.
5. STATUTORY OFFICERS: IT IS RESOLVED that [DIRECTOR A] is appointed Chairperson of the board and that [OFFICER NAME] is appointed Company Secretary, with the duties set out in the constitution and applicable law. The board acknowledges that directors must act in good faith, in the best interests of the Company, and with due care, skill, and diligence under s 189 of the Companies Act 1993.
6. TAX AND CUSTOMS AUTHORITY: IT IS RESOLVED that the directors are authorised to apply for an IRD number, Goods and Services Tax registration, New Zealand Customs client code, and any import/export or environmental licences required for the trade in recycled and shredded non-ferrous scrap, and to retain solicitors, accountants, and planning advisors as necessary. All actions lawfully taken by such advisors within the scope of this resolution are ratified.
This resolution shall remain in full force and effect until the board passes a further resolution amending or revoking it. The directors are jointly and severally directed to register all statutory instruments and to execute all documents necessary for the performance of this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and Companies Register pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-clearance search of the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed corporate name is available, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name, and does not contain a prohibited expression. Submit the online name reservation application through the Companies Office portal, pay the applicable fee, and record the reservation reference number. The application must also confirm that the ordinary business description for ISIC 4669, namely cross-border physical consignment of shredded non-ferrous scrap, is accurate and will not mislead. At least two fallback names should be submitted to reduce processing delays.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two fallback names
Declaration that the name contains no prohibited element
Short business scope narrative for ISIC 4669
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office objects to the proposed name as confusingly similar or prohibited, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request within 5 working days, or alternatively reserve and file one of the fallback names. No court proceedings are necessary at this preliminary stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office portal with the reserved name reference and complete the online incorporation application. Attach the executed constitution, consent to act as director from each director, registered office confirmation, and initial shareholder statement. Verify that each director is not disqualified and has signed the required certificate concerning the Company's ability to pay its debts. Submit the application and pay the official incorporation fee. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and automatically assign a New Zealand Business Number. All statutory particulars on the Companies Register must be reviewed and corrected before the Company commences trading.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director signed by each director
Certified copy of passport or national identification for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or suspends the incorporation, the applicant shall respond within 10 working days through the Companies Office portal, providing the requested amendment, correction, or statutory declaration. Where registration is refused, the incorporator may apply for internal review by the Companies Office and thereafter pursue judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue, GST, and New Zealand Customs registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand Customs Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation to apply for an IRD number and GST registration through the Inland Revenue Department. Because the business will conduct cross-border physical consignment of shredded non-ferrous scrap, the directors must also apply to New Zealand Customs Service for a client code and register for export declarations. Provide the Company's registered office address, bank account details, director identification, and projected turnover. Maintain accounting records sufficient to support GST returns, export documents, and documentary letter of credit transactions. Complete these registrations immediately after incorporation to avoid penalties for late filing or unregistered exporting.
required_dossiers: Proposed bank mandate or bank account details
Projected annual turnover and export volumes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue or Customs queries the application, respond through myIR or the Customs portal with a statutory declaration confirming the exact nature and volume of scrap copper wire transactions. If a deadline is missed, apply for an extension under the Tax Administration Act 1994 rather than submitting an incomplete or false return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Scrap metal dealer licence and police vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Police Licensing and Vetting Branch and Ministry of Justice under the Secondhand Dealers and Pawnbrokers Act 2004
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company must obtain a Scrap Metal Dealer's Licence because it will deal in recycled and scrap non-ferrous metals. Identify the natural person responsible for managing the licensed activity and submit that person's application for a secondhand dealer licence together with the company licence application. Complete the police vetting and disclosure process, including any criminal history, bankruptcy, or prior regulatory matters. Provide the physical premises details, including the scrap storage yard, and demonstrate that the business will record seller identification, maintain a transaction register, and retain records for audit. The licence must be displayed at the registered trading premises and all purchases and consignments must be documented.
required_dossiers: Passport and driver licence of the officer in charge
Police vetting questionnaire and sworn declaration
Photographs and site plan of scrap storage yard
Policies for seller identification and transaction recording
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If police vetting or the licensing decision is challenged, the applicant may request reconsideration through the licensing authority, supply character references and a sworn explanation of disclosures, and, if refused, appeal to the District Court within 28 days of the notice of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Resource consent and environmental compliance for scrap storage and transhipment yard
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Council and territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a planning consultant to prepare an Assessment of Environmental Effects for the operation of the shredded scrap copper storage and consignment yard. File a resource consent application with the relevant council if the activity involves stormwater discharge, noise above district plan thresholds, dust generation, heavy vehicle movement, or storage beyond permitted activity standards. The AEE must address site drainage, spill containment, fire risk, vulnerable waters, air emissions, and waste management. Where the activity is classified as discretionary, public or limited notification may occur. No physical operations may commence until the resource consent is granted or a written permitted activity confirmation is issued.
required_dossiers: Site plan and certificate of title
Stormwater management and spill containment plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the consent authority requests further information, respond within 15 working days or apply for an extension under the Resource Management Act 1991. If consent is declined, request a council hearing and, after the hearing, appeal to the Environment Court within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, AML/CFT enhanced due diligence, and trade finance facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand bank under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate transaction account with a registered New Zealand bank. Present the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, scrap metal dealer licence, director identification, and beneficial ownership declaration. Complete a customer due diligence questionnaire and an enhanced risk assessment because the business is classified as medium risk and will use documentary letters of credit and SWIFT TT payment rails. Provide source-of-funds evidence for initial share capital and projected cash flow forecasts for export sales. If documentary credits and trade finance are required, submit a separate trade finance facility application and obtain the bank's compliance approval before commencing transactions.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership and control structure chart
AML/CFT risk questionnaire and source of funds statement
Sample commercial invoice and draft documentary letter of credit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the application or makes a suspicious activity report, the Company may provide independent verification of beneficial ownership, audited financial statements, and trade contracts. If no resolution is reached, escalate to the bank's internal compliance review, then to the Banking Ombudsman under the applicable consumer or business banking scheme.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Police Licensing and Vetting Branch, Ministry for the Environment, relevant Regional Council, territorial authority, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Scrap Metal Dealer's Licence under the Secondhand Dealers and Pawnbrokers Act 2004, together with any required resource consent and industrial discharge approval for a scrap metal storage and transhipment yard under the Resource Management Act 1991

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Environment and relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Assessment of Environmental Effects and Discretionary Resource Consent are required for a commercial scrap metal storage and transhipment yard that handles stormwater discharge, dust, noise, or heavy vehicle movements above permitted thresholds. A small and fully bunded storage area with no discharge may be treated as a Permitted or Controlled activity under the applicable district and regional plans.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Stormwater discharge must not create an oil or grease sheen and shall meet pH 6-9 and total suspended solids below 100 mg/L at the point of discharge. No untreated wastewater may be discharged to water. Hazardous wastes, including capacitors, oils, and any items containing persistent organic pollutants, must be segregated, stored in covered secondary containment, and removed by a licensed contractor. VOC emissions from material recovery machinery must remain below 2 kg/hr unless captured and treated. Ambient PM10 must not exceed 50 micrograms per cubic metre as a 24-hour average under the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality. All waste handling must comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire safety inspection and evacuation scheme approval, territorial authority building warrant of fitness and structural load inspection for racked scrap storage, and a Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace safety clearance covering confined spaces, manual handling, personal protective equipment, spill response, hazardous substances location compliance, and emergency shutdown procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; online portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident limited company must first complete any applicable New Zealand Companies Register requirement (or register as an overseas company) only if it has a place of business in New Zealand. For tax registration, the entity must apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number. The application can be submitted electronically through the myIR portal after establishing an account as a non-resident company, or by completing the non-resident company IRD-number application form. The company must provide its certificate of incorporation (in English or translated), director particulars, a New Zealand registered address or agent's address, and a statement describing its proposed taxable activity (e.g., export of recycled copper waste and scrap). Once the IRD number is issued, a separate GST registration can be made through the same myIR profile, either before or upon exceeding the NZD 60,000 threshold; registration is advisable earlier if the company wishes to zero-rate exports and reclaim input GST on acquisitions used for export.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available; hybrid mismatch rules operate by statute rather than election. However, an eligible close-held limited company may irrevocably elect look-through company (LTC) status under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to closely held criteria, and a group of wholly owned companies may elect consolidated tax group treatment under subpart IG of the Income Tax Act 2007. These are the only statutory elections affecting tax classification in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any rolling 12-month period (including a reasonable expectation of exceeding the threshold in the next 12 months)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time transaction clearance, fiscal digital stamping, or anti-fraud API submission regime. Electronic invoicing is voluntary, with a PEPPOL-based e-invoicing framework available. GST returns (IR372) must be filed electronically via myIR at the filing frequency determined by IRD; invoices must contain the statutory details set out in the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier has exported, or is responsible for exporting, the goods from New Zealand and the goods are physically removed from New Zealand within 60 days of supply (or within such longer period as the Commissioner accepts). For fragmented non-ferrous scrap (e.g., recycled copper wire), the zero-rating applies on the supply to the overseas buyer if the goods are containerised and shipped under documentary credit or telegraphic transfer, and documentary evidence demonstrates the goods left New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export entry lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (requires accurate classification, value, and destination details for the scrap copper wire)
Bill of lading (or air waybill) signed by the carrier and dated after export, evidencing ship or aircraft departure from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and contract of sale showing the foreign buyer and Incoterms (e.g., FOB, CIF)

Bank settlement confirmation (e.g., SWIFT MT103 or letter of credit presentation) if foreign exchange is repatriated; though not a statutorily required document for zero-rating, it should be retained as underlying evidence of an export sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit the substantiation of export zero-rating by requesting the documents in the bundle above plus associated weight, assay, and container tracking records. If the zero-rating is disallowed, GST at 15% is assessed on the supply, with use-of-money interest accruing from the original due date. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, civil shortfall penalties apply: 20% for failure to take reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position; 40% for gross carelessness or blatant disregard; and 150% for evasion or an arrangement to defraud the revenue. There is no separate foreign-exchange repatriation deadline in New Zealand tax law, but consistent commercial payment records reduce the risk of reconsideration of the export character of the supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Pūtea Matua
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a freely convertible currency with no general exchange control restrictions. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) trades freely on the spot, forward, and swap markets. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) does not impose exchange controls under the Currency (Restrictions of Use) Act or the Overseas Investment Act, except for notifications on very large investments or fisheries/quota assets. Capital account transactions for resident and non-resident investors are fully liberalised. There are no surrender requirements for export earnings, and companies may hold foreign currency accounts at registered banks without RBNZ approval. Dividends and capital repatriations follow standard company law and tax clearance procedures, not FX authorisation. The practical hurdle is not convertibility but rather the exchange rate risk and bank AML/KYC requirements for high-risk commodity trades such as scrap copper. Profit remittance is straightforward with a completed IR4/IR7 tax form and bank FX contract. For a limited company engaged in recycling of non-ferrous scrap metal, the RBNZ expects all overseas direct investment to be reported for statistical purposes via Statistics New Zealand's overseas direct investment survey, but this is not a permission gate. Overall, the regime is one of the most open in the OECD, with no administrative ceilings on current or capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts under New Zealand law. Exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in foreign currency accounts held with registered banks, or convert to NZD at commercial rates. The only compliance obligation is accurate record-keeping for GST, customs valuation, and tax purposes. For ISIC 4669 scrap metal trading, exporters should document the underlying export declaration and lodgement to Customs NZ to reconcile with FX receipts for banks' AML monitoring.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and NZD Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (Commonwealth Bank of Australia Group)

NZD Transaction Account and USD Settlement Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, or Revolut Business) operate in New Zealand either as money remitters under the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) or via banking-as-a-service partnerships with registered banks. They are legally permitted to service NZ-domiciled entities, but they are not Registered Banks and cannot issue documentary letters of credit, negotiate bills of exchange, or offer trade finance credit. For the specific scope of recycled scrap copper wire trading—which is a medium-risk enhanced commodity with high-value cross-border flows—the practical viability of an EMI as the primary treasury rail is Low to Medium. EMIs can provide an on-ramp for Fiat collection, debit cards, and basic SWIFT transfers, but they often apply strict velocity controls on high-value metals traders, request full downstream paperwork on every transaction, and may close accounts if the trade involves tier-3 jurisdictions. Moreover, offshore EMIs without an NZ FMA licence cannot provide a local NZD IBAN necessary for local clearing (NZ Clearing, ESAS). Therefore, for LC settlements and multi-million dollar consignment, a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank is mandatory. An EMI may be used only as a secondary collection tool for pre-payments under USD 20,000, with full audit trails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the statutory directors of a New Zealand limited company are not generally required to appear physically in-branch if the bank can complete non-face-to-face customer due diligence using certified copies of identity documents and a company extract from the New Zealand Companies Register. However, for a medium-risk enhanced business such as ISIC 4669 (scrap metal trading), most major banks will require at least one director or a nominated beneficial owner to attend a video-identification interview conducted by the bank's AML compliance officer, or to attend in person at a designated branch if the relationship includes trade facilities. Remote consular proxy opening is permissible only if the director signs a statutory declaration before a NZ consular officer or a notary public, and that declaration is transmitted directly to the bank's compliance team. For bank accounts requiring an FX credit facility or documentary LC, the bank will almost always impose a physical presence visit by the relationship manager to the business premises or a registered office inspection, especially if the annual throughput exceeds NZD 1 million. We recommend budgeting for a senior director to be available in Auckland for a one-day onboarding interview, and for the ultimate beneficial owner to provide police clearance certificates from their country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic routing: Scrap copper sourced from or transit through jurisdictions with known circumvention of import/export controls (e.g., Middle East free zones, certain Asian transshipment hubs).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete supply chain traceability package: (1) original supplier invoice and packing list; (2) direct vessel or air waybill to New Zealand without transshipment, or a justified transshipment bill showing the previous port and surrender of the original bill; (3) certificate of origin for the scrap; (4) customs import entry and quarantine inspection certificate from New Zealand Customs/Biosecurity NZ; (5) EPA shipping manifest; (6) a notarised letter from the overseas supplier confirming the source of the scrap (e.g., decommissioned electrical infrastructure, automotive recycling) and beneficial ownership of the supplier. The bank will also request the end-customer's export licence from the origin country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant mismatch between reported purchase price of shredded copper wire and prevailing LME copper price, indicating possible trade-based money laundering or invoice manipulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a dated pricing model: (1) LME Copper Grade A settlement price on the invoice date; (2) a certified assay report from an independent sorter or SGS equivalent showing the copper content percentage of the shredded wire, including the scrap grade (e.g., milberry, candy); (3) a professional valuation report from a chartered engineer or certified scrap inspector; (4) the full cost build-up (collection, shredding, transport, insurance) to justify any deviation from LME benchmark; (5) audited financial statements and the underlying purchase contract from the domestic NZ supplier. Banks compare transaction value against customs declaration and insurance value; all three must reconcile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-financial beneficial ownership or nominee director structure obscuring the ultimate controller of NZ_LTD, especially with trust involvement (Offshore Trust protection) for a physical commodity trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a corporate organisation chart certified by an NZ registered chartered accountant, naming all shareholders, directors, and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) with passport copies. Include: (1) the trust deed of any offshore trust and a trustee resolution authorising the trading activity; (2) a clean criminal record certificate from the UBO's country of residence; (3) source of wealth questionnaire concerning the initial capital injection (including bank statements from the funding bank); (4) a written AML/CFT compliance declaration by the company's compliance officer and the adoption of a risk management programme per the AML/CFT Act; (5) disclosure of any PEP (politically exposed person) relationships; (6) a board resolution specifically authorising the opening of the account and the designated trade approvers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual settlement pattern for scrap copper, such as payment to a third-party factoring firm, or heavy use of cash withdrawals, or rapid round-tripping of funds between the NZ account and foreign accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide for each relevant transaction: (1) the original commercial contract and the addendum identifying the payment chain; (2) bank statements from all related accounts showing that the third-party is a disclosed financial intermediary such as a commodity factoring house with a valid licence; (3) a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the intermediary, supported by the interest/fee agreement; (4) a sworn affidavit from the directors that no cash payments have been accepted; (5) a signed head of terms with the final buyer and the LC issuance bank confirming that the final settlement will be through documentary LC. For recurring wire transfers, submit a 12-month projected cash flow forecast with expected debits and credits, so that the bank's transaction monitoring can establish a baseline.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound equity capital into NZ_LTD from an offshore shareholder, the standard routing is a SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code 'Direct investment in New Zealand' (World Bank remittance code 901 or NZD external capital code DCX). The funds are settled into a separate Capital Escrow Account (also known as an incoming funds account) at the Tier-1 bank. There is no exchange control permission for capital injection, but the bank will require: (1) the share subscription agreement; (2) the company constitution and resolution of directors; (3) the shareholder's identity and evidence of funds; (4) confirmation of the New Zealand Inland Revenue (IRD) non-resident withholding tax registration for future dividends. After the funds are cleared, the bank will transfer the amount to the operating account under a 'Foreign Direct Investment - Equity' reference. For capital verification under New Zealand Companies Act, a chartered accountant must provide a certificate confirming the amount received and credited to the share capital account within 20 working days. If the injection exceeds NZD 5 million in any 12-month rolling period, the Investment Screening Office (Overseas Investment Act) may require approval, although the scrap metal trading business itself typically qualifies for the 'substantial business assets' exception if less than NZD 100 million. Any conversion from AUD or USD to NZD will be executed at the bank's custodian rate, with an option to fix the rate via a forward contract on the day of the wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Given the target payment rails of Documentary LC and Swift TT, the recommended clearing structure is as follows: (1) For export sales of shredded scrap copper, the primary settlement rail is a SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers from overseas buyers when transaction size is below USD 1 million, with the bank's reference for goods export (World Bank purpose code 101) to ensure stable clearing. (2) For larger consignments, the bank will issue an Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (LC) on behalf of NZ_LTD as the beneficiary, or negotiate an LC received from the buyer's bank. Under an LC, the bank will require presentation of a full set of clean-on-board bills of lading, commercial invoice, weight certificate and assay certificate, packing list, and a certificate of origin. Settlement will occur at the counters of the negotiating bank within New Zealand, and proceeds will be credited to the company's NZD account after the usual 2-business-day collection period. (3) For purchases from domestic collectors, the bank may offer Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for smaller suppliers, but for a treasury blueprint we recommend using NZD direct cash settlement via the clearing system (ESAS) with same-day funds for domestic vendors, and using MT103 with USD for overseas suppliers. (4) To reduce bank fees and FX spreads, the company should hold a multi-currency balance in NZD, USD, AUD, and CNY. All outbound wires must pass through the bank's AML filters, and the bank will require the purpose code 'Trade payment - export proceeds' or 'Payment for imported goods' on each instruction. The bank also requires that the physical shipping documents be submitted within 7 days of shipment for trade reconciliation to avoid a potential freeze under FATF recommendation 16.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD) with settlement at maturity, permitted under the bank's standard ISDA/CSA or individual master agreement, provided the underlying exposure is a genuine commercial trade contract for scrap copper.

Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD) to convert long-term financing or capital injection proceeds, permitted for hedging the principal and interest of foreign-currency loans, subject to a board resolution describing the underlying debt.

FX plain-vanilla options (call or put) on NZD/USD to protect the sales price of the export load without eliminating upside, permitted when the notional amount does not exceed 100% of projected quarterly export sales and the option is designated as a cash flow hedge.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for settlement of receivables in restricted Asian currencies (e.g., CNY in offshore markets) where physical delivery is not possible; for USD/NZD NDFs are uncommon and generally not recommended due to the full convertibility of NZD and the availability of deliverable markets, though the bank may allow an NDF if the counterparty is in a jurisdiction with remittance restrictions, provided the NDF is macro-hedged against the trade receivable.

Commodity-linked forward price swaps that lock the LME copper price to the scrap value are permissible if executed through the bank's derivatives desk, but these should be treated as commodity derivatives requiring a separate risk disclosure under the Financial Markets Conduct Act and are outside pure FX hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Act 1993 Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 working days after the company's annual return date, which is normally the anniversary of incorporation; for a company incorporated on 31 March, the annual return is due no later than approximately 6 May, calculated on working days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approximately USD 60) in addition to the base annual return fee of NZD 45 (approximately USD 27). Continued failure to file, after formal notice by the Registrar, is a ground for removal of the company from the New Zealand Companies Register under sections 318 to 320 of the Companies Act 1993, resulting in strike-off, loss of legal capacity, and vesting of remaining assets in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and, where compulsory, independent certified auditor's report to shareholders and to the Companies Office for large or FMC reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directors and shareholders; for large or Financial Markets Conduct Act FMC reporting entities, also filed with the Companies Office under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must prepare financial statements within 5 months after balance date; for a 31 March balance date, by 31 August. A signed statutory audit report, when required, must accompany the financial statements before they are presented to shareholders at the annual meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-preparation, non-audit, or non-filing is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Companies Act 1993, with director-level fines up to NZD 50,000 on conviction. Continued non-compliance may be enforced by court order, director disqualification, and, for large or overseas-owned companies, strike-off from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company income tax return (IR4) for the New Zealand tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Te Tari Tauhake, New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, file by 7 July following balance date unless an extension of time is granted to a tax agent; for non-standard balance dates, the statutory due date is the last working day of the third month after the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for companies; late payment penalties of 1% per month on overdue tax, with incremental penalties up to 10%; statutory use-of-money interest at IRD's prescribed rate; and possible prosecution, director personal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and IRD debt-enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and services tax (GST) returns for each taxable period, including the final annual reconciliation where the company files on a six-monthly basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: GST returns are due one month after the end of the taxable period; for a six-monthly filer with a 31 March balance date, the final GST return for the year ended 31 March is due by 7 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: IRD attaches a late filing penalty of NZD 250 per GST return, plus late payment penalties of 1% per month on the overdue GST and continuing default penalties, and use-of-money interest at IRD's prescribed rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe benefit tax (FBT) annual return or quarterly FBT returns where the company provides fringe benefits to employees or associated persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly FBT returns are due by the 20th of the month following the quarter; an annual FBT filing election for employers with annual taxable fringe benefits of NZD 2,000 or less must be made by 20 May after a 31 March year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts the IRD late filing penalty of NZD 250, late payment penalties of up to 10% of the tax, and use-of-money interest at IRD's prescribed rate; continued default may also trigger debt collection and director personal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory where the New Zealand company is: (i) an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, such as a listed issuer, registered bank, licensed insurer, or manager of a managed investment scheme; (ii) a large for-profit entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 / XRB A1 framework, applying the statutory tests based on total assets exceeding NZD 60 million at balance date or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million for the reporting period, and any applicable 50 full-time-equivalent employee limb; (iii) a large overseas-owned subsidiary or a subsidiary of a large overseas parent; or (iv) required by shareholder resolution, constitution, lender covenant, or an IRD notice to produce audited financial statements. Small proprietary companies that do not meet those thresholds and are not FMC reporting entities may avoid a compulsory statutory audit where the shareholders have properly approved the audit-exemption election.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) applying the XRB standards framework: Tier 1 uses New Zealand International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS); Tier 2 uses NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); smaller for-profit entities that are not large and do not have public accountability may use Tier 3 Simple Format Reporting Accrual, or Tier 4 Simple Format Reporting Cash for the smallest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO annual return on the Companies Register. The annual return filed with the Companies Office confirms the registered shareholders and directors at the annual return date. Share transfers and share issues must be promptly recorded in the company's own Register of Members; changes of directors and registered office must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days; and for regulated entities such as a medium-risk enhanced scrap-metal trader, any material change in beneficial ownership or control must be reported within the applicable 30-working-day AML/CFT notification window to the relevant AML/CFT supervisor under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, with refreshed ongoing customer due diligence.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,200 per annum for a licensed registered agent / registered office service in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a full certified statutory audit; small-company review or agreed-upon-procedures engagements range from USD 4,000 - USD 10,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday, territorial exemption, patent box, or preferential free-zone corporate income tax rate exists in the New Zealand unitary tax system. The effective tax rate can be reduced through the 15% refundable Research and Development Tax Incentive, imputation credits that preserve the single-level tax principle, accelerated depreciation for recycling plant and machinery, and deductions for environmental remediation; these incentives require genuine economic activity and are unavailable to shell or conduit companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR, together with the IR10 financial statement schedule and supporting transfer pricing and shareholder continuity schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed on or before 7 July of the following income year; where a non-standard balance date is adopted, the filing date is generally the 6th day of the second month after balance date, unless a tax agent extension has been granted by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from all sources: sales of recycled shredded scrap copper wire, export proceeds, commissions, exchange gains, and any other assessable income. A New Zealand resident company is taxed on worldwide income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full gross contract value of every export sale supported by sales invoices, bills of lading, letters of credit, and SWIFT settlement advice. Convert all foreign currency income into NZD using Inland Revenue exchange-rate rules. Do not net intercompany purchases, freight, insurance, or handling charges against gross sales. Cross-border related-party invoicing must be disclosed on the contemporaneous transfer pricing schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: scrap purchase cost, freight, port handling, inspection, insurance, storage, customs duties, bank charges, and all expenses incurred in deriving assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only for expenses genuinely incurred in producing assessable income and paid on arm's length terms. For scrap copper purchases from non-resident related suppliers, maintain local file evidence of comparability, customs valuations, and payment flows. Payments to non-resident connected parties may be subject to non-resident withholding tax if characterised as interest, royalties, or deemed distributions; deductions are denied if the withholding tax obligations are not properly discharged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax per financial statements, used as the reconciliation starting point between accounting profit and taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile statutory accounting profit to tax profit by adding back non-deductible fines, illegal payments, 50% of entertainment expenses, and any amount attributable to an arrangement tainted by the general anti-avoidance rule. Deduct only properly documented foreign-source income that is exempt under a double tax agreement; ordinary trading income of an NZ company remains assessable in New Zealand even where the counterparty is offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses utilised: loss carry-forward from prior years, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity requirement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If non-resident beneficial ownership of shares changed by more than 51% between the loss year and the utilisation year, the loss is extinguished. Attach shareholder registers, nominee declarations, trust beneficiary schedules, and continuity declarations. A loss from a non-resident entity is never available unless validly merged into the NZ tax group under a statutory amalgamation or branch election; losses are denied where the continuity of beneficial shareholders falls below 49%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: imputation credits attached to dividends received, foreign withholding tax credits, resident withholding tax credits, and supplementary dividend credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not obtain a cash refund of imputation credits because NRWT is charged on the gross dividend distribution to the non-resident. The NZ company must report its imputation credit account balance on the imputation return and cannot attach imputation credits to a dividend paid to a non-resident simply to extinguish NRWT. Foreign tax credits should be claimed only where the corresponding foreign income has been included in taxable income and New Zealand is the residence state for crediting purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and tax calculation at the 28% company rate; residual income tax is the final tax payable after allowable credits and terminal tax instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory 28% corporate rate to taxable income. This is not a gross-receipts tax. If the Commissioner adjusts transfer pricing under section GC 13 of the Income Tax Act 2007, the adjusted profit is reflected in this box and attracts use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties from the original return due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident schedules: dividends paid to non-residents, NRWT payable on those dividends, payments of interest and royalties to non-residents, and disclosure of the treaty relief position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule showing the name, jurisdiction, tax identification number, tax residency certificate, beneficial ownership status, and treaty withholding rate of each non-resident payee. If the reduced DTA rate is applied, the payer must hold the completed Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration before the payment date. If documentation is incomplete, NRWT must be withheld at the full statutory rates: 30% on dividends and 15% on interest and royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declarations and director certification of the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The director must certify that the return is true and complete, that related-party transactions are at arm's length, that no arrangement has a dominant purpose of tax avoidance, that economic substance exists in New Zealand, and that all material cross-border payments and non-resident beneficiary details have been disclosed. A false certification converts a civil exposure into criminal evasion exposure for the director personally.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers an initial late-filing penalty of NZD 250 plus continuing late-filing penalties until the return is filed; late payment of residual income tax triggers late-payment penalties at 1% per month and compounding use-of-money interest. A knowingly incorrect return attracts tax shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 ranging from 10% for failure to take reasonable care up to 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution for evasion under section 143B exposes the company and directors to fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years; fraudulent GST refund claims are prosecuted as tax fraud with the same criminal ceiling.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: New Zealand imposes Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at 30% on gross dividends paid by the NZ company to a non-resident recipient. Imputation credits do not reduce this statutory NRWT on outbound dividends; they are directed by the New Zealand resident shareholder credit mechanism, not by the non-resident withholding code. Under an applicable Double Tax Agreement, the dividend NRWT may be reduced to 15% in the general case and to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the voting power, subject to substantive ownership and economic substance conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on an outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payment, the non-resident payee must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the domestic revenue authority of its residence state, complete the Inland Revenue prescribed treaty rate reduction declaration and NRWT return schedule, and provide a beneficial ownership statement confirming that the payee is not a conduit or nominee. The NZ payer must receive these documents before the payment is made, must withhold at the reduced treaty rate only if all procedural conditions are satisfied, must retain the documentation for seven years, and must attach a full non-resident payee disclosure to the IR4 and NRWT returns. If the documents are absent, the payer must withhold at the statutory rate and no retrospective correction is available except through a refund application by the non-resident beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The full statutory NRWT rate for cross-border interest and royalties is 15% each. Typical DTA protocols reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10%, with certain copyright royalties and technical service royalties reduced to 0% or 5% depending on the treaty and the nature of the IP income. Interest payments to non-resident related lenders are also tested under thin capitalisation rules; excessive debt is recharacterised as equity so that the interest becomes a deemed dividend subject to 30% NRWT. Royalties paid to non-residents are deductible only if the IP is genuinely used in the New Zealand business and the amount is arm's length; back-to-back licence arrangements without real use or substance are attacked under the general anti-avoidance rule.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No hard statutory monetary threshold in the Income Tax Act 2007 automatically requires preparation of a Local File or Master File; however, Inland Revenue administrative practice and OECD-aligned transfer pricing guidelines require taxpayers to prepare contemporaneous documentation for all connected-party cross-border transactions, with an expectation of formal Local File and Master File documentation where annual related-party dealings exceed NZD 1,000,000. The Commissioner may require documents and particulars under the Tax Administration Act 1994 sections 16 and 17 where material related-party copper scrap transactions are present, and failure to substantiate the arm's length price shifts the evidentiary burden against the taxpayer.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate named Economic Substance Regulations comparable to zero-tax offshore jurisdictions; nevertheless, the Income Tax Act 2007 general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1, the transfer pricing rule in section GC 13, and double tax agreement substance doctrines require the NZ entity to prove real business purpose, physical premises, employees, board control, and core income-generating activities in the scrap copper purchase, grading, shredding, logistics, and resale chain. A company without substance that exists solely to collect treaty benefits or to re-invoice non-ferrous scrap transactions is treated as a sham and can be reconstructed, denied treaty relief, assessed on deemed profits, and subjected to director personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of shredded scrap copper wire export revenue on the IR4 by creating false supplier purchase orders to inflate cost of goods sold, by settling sales in cash outside bank records, by routing receipts through an offshore nominee account, and by filing GST returns that claim fabricated input credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalties under Tax Administration Act 1994 sections 141A-141E of up to 150% of the evaded tax plus use-of-money interest; criminal prosecution under section 143B for evasion carries a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. A false GST refund claim is prosecuted separately as tax fraud under the same statutory regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knew of or directed the fraudulent scheme is treated as a principal offender. The court may pierce the corporate veil under Companies Act 1990 section 588 to hold the director personally liable for all tax debts and trade creditor losses arising from dishonest trading. The director's personal assets can be frozen, alternative family trust assets traced, travel restricted by border alert/blacklisting while the case is pending, and upon conviction the director faces up to 5 years imprisonment, restitution orders, and disqualification from managing any New Zealand company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the New Zealand Ltd as an invoice-only shell with no physical office, no scrap copper inventory, no employees, no local bank account, no board minutes, and no commercial decision-making, solely to route circular non-ferrous metal sales through New Zealand to access treaty withholding rate reductions and to disguise the foreign parent as the seller of record.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reconstruction under Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1 and section GB 1; transfer pricing adjustment under section GC 13; denial of DTA benefits; assessment of the offshore profit in the hands of the NZ company or the real controller; imposition of 30% NRWT on deemed distributions; and tax shortfall penalties for an unacceptable tax position up to 40%, rising to 150% if the shell arrangement is held to be evasive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who lend their names without undertaking real functions are personally exposed where they knowingly participate in a sham. Under Companies Act 1990 sections 383 and 588, directors may be personally accountable for company debts, stripped of limited liability protection, ordered to pay restitution, prohibited from acting as directors, and placed on border alert/blacklisting while asset recovery is pursued. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent use of corporate documents can result in imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF and Trade-Based Money Laundering / Export Misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mis-invoicing non-ferrous scrap copper wire by over- or under-valuing export prices between related entities; layering proceeds through multiple Swift T/T and documentary L/C payments routed through shell bank accounts in high-risk jurisdictions; concealing the true origin of the scrap; failing to obtain the required statutory export licence; and using a recycled copper wire consignment as a covert payment channel to move funds for or on behalf of sanctioned persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 civil penalties of up to NZD 2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZD 400,000 for an individual; Customs and Excise Act 2018 penalties and forfeiture of goods for false export declarations; and criminal prosecution under Crimes Act 1961 section 243 for money laundering, punishable by imprisonment for up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who controls or directs the payment chain is liable as a principal participant in the laundering exercise. The director's personal and family trust assets are subject to confiscation under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009; the director may be refused departure from New Zealand through border alert/blacklisting mechanisms; upon conviction the director faces up to 7 years imprisonment, recovery of assets traceable to the offending, and a permanent ban from holding director positions in any New Zealand company.
